Ala pyta: „Co masz?” Jan odpowiada: „Mam rysunek.” Teraz Jan pyta: „Ty? Co masz?” Ala odpowiada: „Mam kartkę, nie rysunek.” Ewa pokazuje kartkę i mówi: „Tu jest napis: Brak. Nie ma lampy.” Ala czyta napis. Jan nie szuka kartki. Patrzy tam: półka.

Jan pokazuje półkę. Pyta: „Czy widzisz lampę?” Ala patrzy i mówi: „Nie widzę lampy. Widzę półkę.” Jan bierze rysunek i pokazuje lampę. Ala mówi: „Tu widzę lampę, ale to jest papier.” Jan kładzie rysunek i pokazuje okno. Jest dzień. Teraz Ala widzi napis i literę.

Ala kładzie kartkę tu. Jan nie bierze rysunku. Bierze kartkę i czyta: Lampa. Brak. Teraz Ala nie ma kartki. Jan ma kartkę. Ala pokazuje papier i pyta: „Kto ma kartkę?” Ewa pokazuje kartkę. Jan odpowiada: „Ja. Teraz ja mam kartkę.”

grammar.title: Gramatyka
grammar.rule: Ja mam. Ty masz. Jan ma. Czy masz? Mam. Kto ma kartkę?
grammar.note_en:
Person tells us who performs an action. The first person singular is the speaker, “I”; the second person singular is the one person being addressed, “you”. Polish ja means “I”, and ty means familiar singular “you”. Ala and Jan are friends, so this form is appropriate. The person changes when the speaker changes: ja is Ala in one turn and Jan in another. It is not a permanent name for either character.

The present tense describes what happens now or is generally true. Polish normally uses one present form where English may use either a simple present or “am/is/are …ing”. Mam means “I have”; masz means “you have”; the earlier ma means “has”. Ja mam kartkę / Ty masz rysunek / Jan ma rysunek means “I have the note / You have the drawing / Jan has the drawing”. In context the verb ending usually identifies the person, so mam and ja mam are both possible. The story includes ja and ty where contrasting speakers or correcting a mistaken holder matters. Do not add an English-style separate “am” before an action verb.

Learn the actual present forms of each verb; do not attach one ending to every infinitive. Compare widzę / widzisz / widzi (“I see / you see / sees”), szukam / szukasz / szuka (“I look for / you look for / looks for”), and rysuję / rysujesz / rysuje (“I draw / you draw / draws”). Rysuję has final ę in the first person; rysuje without that final mark is third person. The same contrast occurs in widzę and widzi, but their stems differ too. The tables list only forms already read, not full conjugations.

Changing person does not remove the noun-case patterns already learned. Mam kartkę means “I have the note”; Nie mam kartki means “I do not have the note”. Widzę półkę / Nie widzę lampy means “I see the shelf / I do not see the lamp”. Szukam lampy / Szukasz lampy means “I am looking for the lamp / You are looking for the lamp”: positive search still takes the genitive. Rysuję półkę means “I am drawing the shelf”. The subject pronouns ja and ty remain in their naming forms; personal object pronouns are not introduced here.

Czy can introduce a direct yes/no question without changing the verb into a special question form. Czy masz kartkę? means “Do you have the note?” Mam means “I do”; Nie mam kartki means “I do not have the note”. Co masz? means “What do you have?”; Co rysujesz? means “What are you drawing?” Kto ma kartkę? means “Who has the note?”: kto asks for the person and takes the third-person ma here. The answer identifies a person rather than merely saying yes or no. Gdzie jest lampa? remains the familiar direct “Where is the lamp?”; these are not indirect clauses embedded after another verb.

The mental verbs distinguish different kinds of information. Wiem / wiesz means “I know / you know”; Pamiętam / pamiętasz means “I remember / you remember”; Rozumiem / rozumiesz means “I understand / you understand”. Wiem. Klucz jest tu means “I know. The key is here”. Nie wiem is an honest “I do not know”, rather than a negative fact about the key itself. Pamiętam lampę means “I remember the lamp”. Rozumiem. Ja szukam tam. Ty szukasz tu means “I understand. I search there. You search here”: Jan now correctly follows the division of the search. Czy pamiętasz? and Czy rozumiesz? mean “Do you remember?” and “Do you understand?” These present verbs do not introduce a past tense. Ewa’s evening recollection is presented directly, with the familiar present sentences inside it.

Mówi means “says/speaks”, pyta “asks”, and odpowiada “answers”. They introduce direct quoted speech: Ala pyta: „Co masz?” means “Ala asks: ‘What do you have?’”; Jan odpowiada: „Mam rysunek” means “Jan answers: ‘I have the drawing’”. No full paradigm of these three verbs is required here. The note records Brak (“missing”), which Ewa explains by Nie ma lampy (“There is no lamp”). A memory prompted by the drawing is a different source of information from that written label.

Two phrases are for recognition only here: cudza koperta means “an envelope belonging to someone else”, and cudza lampa means “a lamp belonging to someone else”. This is about ownership, not whether something is missing or presently held. The known envelope is addressed to Ala, so Ewa calls it cudza koperta from her own perspective. The lamp statement is a newly prompted recollection, not information secretly encoded in Brak. Cudza is the feminine naming form of the adjective whose dictionary label is cudzy. This chapter does not teach the general adjective pattern; that comes in chapter 6. You are not asked to produce cudza in exercises or cards yet.

items.prompt: „Tu i tam”: gdzie szuka Ala? Gdzie szuka Jan?
model_answers: Ala szuka tu, Jan szuka tam.
items.rubric: Give the two agreed different places: Ala checks the shelf and Jan the already-open drawer. Tu/tam with both named actors is valid in the scene’s frame; no lamp is found.

Accept a complete sentence naming the shelf, drawer, or both: Ala draws the shelf first and adds the drawer in s019. This is the separate search sketch on the loose drawer paper; Jan’s existing lamp drawing is a different sheet. No new physical shelf or drawer is built.
A complete sentence may name the lamp or reproduce the accurate evening recollection with Ala holding the note and Jan the drawing. Do not infer that Ewa knows the lamp’s present location.
Name a fact Ewa actually establishes: the written Brak label and absence are recorded. Her prompted recollection is distinguished from that record; no current location or remover is established.

Personal response: give a complete present first-person sentence with rysuję and any taught singular inanimate object in its affirmative object form, for example klucz, półkę or lampę. There is no required personal preference or story fact. If you are not drawing, Nie rysuję is a valid truthful complete response.
